scope: READ-ONLY cause attribution for window-dependent compiled content. No worldgen, map, law or engine change; no option is chosen here.
notes: Each window is read through a QA inspection landing (qaUsed=true) purely so a real RunState and therefore the real blockGrid exists; QA landings are never playable evidence.
H4 is this diagnosis' own footprint (G1B fixtures deploy only inside their own run window) and is reported separately so it is never counted as worldgen.
Frame-wide magnitude is measured independently by global-foot-reachability.audit.test.ts (0.1209% of 49,076,416 overlap readings); this file explains cause on a stratified sample of neighbour pairs.

floors.ground is NOT an independent pre-window layer: buildFloorStack level 0 copies base.tiles and base.sourceV3, and resetWindowToGround copies them straight back. Any world-vs-ground comparison is therefore circular and is asserted away here instead of being reported as a cause.

The padded compile is window-invariant in its anchor lattice but NOT in its inputs: the POIs a window slices are stamped into the padded biome/tile/freshness fields before sources are scattered, so neighbouring windows with different POI slices scatter different sources (cause H1d / pass P6).

The POI pass is window-relative three times over: which POIs a window slices (anchor +/-55 margin plus bbox overlap in slicePoisForWindow), which of a POI's tiles fall inside the window rect, and which of those survive buildFloorStack's stricter 1-tile border clip (which also nulls sources under stamped tiles).

seedIndependence.reading: The compiled window content carries no run seed: the seed affects only which pseudo-random pairs this harness samples and its own G1B fixture deployment (cause H4). A worldgen fix therefore needs validating on one seed, not on a seed sweep.

namedWindowRelativePasses.statement: Sources are placed by a padded compile anchored on GLOBAL chunk centres (window-invariant by intent), then filtered by `if (sk && wReached[i]) sourceV3[i] = sk`, where wReached is the union of reachable() floods from window-LOCAL `compiler_x_y` anchors. The flood stops at the 200x200 border, so a source whose connecting path leaves the box is kept in one window and dropped in the next.
namedWindowRelativePasses.evidenceReading: walkable agrees at every single H1 cell, so the flood difference cannot come from local geometry: it comes from where the flood starts and where the window border stops it.

namedWindowRelativePasses.statement: A POI is stamped three times with three different window-relative clips: slicePoisForWindow drops tiles outside the window rect, the padded compile drops tiles outside the 216x216 padded rect, and buildFloorStack applies a stricter 1-tile inner border clip (and nulls any source under a stamped tile). A POI straddling a window edge is therefore a different shape in each window.
namedWindowRelativePasses.evidenceReading: every sampled tile difference lies within 2 tiles of a window border, which is the border-clip signature; no interior tile difference was found.

namedWindowRelativePasses.statement: Interior dressing is decided per window: interior.ts hashes WINDOW-LOCAL x,y (hash(x,y,7|11|13|23)) to choose piers, partitions and furniture, its pier grid is anchored on the local origin (a 64-tile slide shifts a 6-tile grid by 4), landmark props are clipped to the window rect by slicePoisForWindow and then rejected within 2 tiles of the border by canPlaceProceduralSolidProp, and every placement guard (protectedThreshold, wouldSeverFootprint, g1bReserved) is evaluated on window-local geometry. The result lands in FloorLayer.solidProps, which cellClass reads directly (`if (layer.solidProps[i]) c = 2`).
namedWindowRelativePasses.evidenceReading: No static object differs anywhere (staticsKindFlicker is none<->none throughout): only the solidProps flag does. This is the ONLY cause found deep inside both windows, so it is the one that cannot be dismissed as a seam artifact.

namedWindowRelativePasses.statement: spawnEligible is prefiltered by a freshwater BFS that runs on the inner 200x200 arrays only, so the distance field is truncated at the window border. Cells whose class, tile and source all agree still flip spawnEligible between windows.
namedWindowRelativePasses.evidenceReading: Every mask-only difference is spawnEligible and nothing else: walkable, protected, buildable and solidProps agree on all of them. This is invisible to the collision grid but it drives chooseLegalSpawn.

namedWindowRelativePasses.statement: The padded compile is window-invariant in its ANCHOR LATTICE only (global-chunk-aligned `gx % 32 === 16`), not in its inputs: paddedPoiTiles stamps the POIs THIS window sliced into the padded biome/tile/freshness fields the compile then scatters sources over. Neighbouring windows slice different POI sets (anchor +/-55 margin plus bbox overlap), so the scattered source set differs even where both windows' own floods reach the cell.
namedWindowRelativePasses.evidenceReading: Every sampled cell of this kind sits in a pair whose two windows sliced a different POI set. This is the mechanism that defeats the "100% window-invariant source placement" comment, and it is separate from the reachability filter.

quotes.text: if (rules === 4) { placePoiSalvage(ww, poiAt); unplugSalvage(ww); }

namedWindowRelativePasses.statement: Under placement rules 4 (the engine default for every new Veyra run) placePoiSalvage/unplugSalvage run AFTER the reachability filter, so industrial salvage sources are not subject to it and follow POI slicing instead.
namedWindowRelativePasses.evidenceReading: Small (62 cells sampled) but it is the only source mechanism that bypasses the filter entirely.

findings.deepInteriorReading: Cells at least 64 tiles inside BOTH windows cannot be seam artifacts. In this sample every one of them is P3 procedural props.

classSemantics.reading: engine.cellClass assigns class 2 for BOTH a blocking source and a FloorLayer.solidProps cell, so a class 2<->0 flicker is not by itself evidence of a source difference. The earlier frame-wide mosaic read 2<->0 as "blocking source"; that reading was incomplete and is corrected here.

residueNotSubAttributed.reading: These cells are attributed to a layer (H2 tile / H3 solidProps) but lie inside no sliced POI bbox. The bbox test is conservative: a prop footprint or a room detail can reach past the bbox tested here, and the padded compile lets a POI influence cells up to 8 tiles outside the window. They are reported as residue, not as a separate mechanism, and are not claimed to be explained cell by cell.

selfConsistency.reading: All three are zero, so the quoted filter is the operative mechanism for every sampled source difference: no source survives where its own window flood rejects it, and no source is dropped where both windows reach it.
